chapter_title: Concerning the First Man and the Ambassador and the Ship; what they resemble.
chapter_note: A collection of five cosmic parables/similes mapping redemption processes within the cosmic system. Gardner notes the original contexts are lost and these were assembled during transmission. Teaching purity is 1.000 with zero editorial fatigue—the substrate dominates almost completely. Each parable maps a cosmic agent (First Man, Great Spirit, Living Spirit, Ambassador) to a simile figure, with both sides staying within the cosmic system. The only non-substrate material is the final paragraph (¶6), which pivots to exhortation/application directed at the audience. The 'Once again' markers at the head of each parable are minimal editorial collection markers, easily stripped to reveal the teaching underneath. The systematic structure (parable → cosmic referent) is Persian pedagogical tradition: teaching through analogy within the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The First [Man] is like a great distinguished man whose treasure has been taken away from him. He came to pursue his treasure. This is how the [First] Man too came after his sons from the heights, so that he might redeem them and retrieve his treasure, which had been scattered amongst his enemies.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again he speaks:' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The parable maps cosmic entity (First Man) to simile figure (distinguished man pursuing treasure), then explains the cosmic referent (sons = living soul, enemies = powers of Darkness). Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. The 'this is how' connective is the teaching's own explanatory mechanism linking parable to referent. Bridge connective detected by NLP but 'Once again he speaks' is simply the dialogue frame opening for the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: [He is like a man] whose two sons were taken away from him by [ ... He] came out toward them to redeem them. This is how the First Man [ ... ] shines in the heights because of his two sons, who were separated from him. They are his living soul that exist in two powers, which makes four.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again,' at opening — editorial collection marker linking this parable to the sequence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly systematic cosmological content: 'his living soul that exist in two powers, which makes four' is precise degree-structure teaching. The two-becoming-four formula is characteristic of the oldest substrate arithmetic. The 'Again, this is how' connective within the parable links simile to cosmic referent—kept as teaching structure but normalized 'Again' to start fresh sentence. Substrate score 6.35 confirms cosmological vocabulary density.

paragraphs.core_text: The ship [of the day] is like a great spear [ ... ... The Great Spirit too, which is in it, is like a wise [crafts]man who might beautify and set aright [all] the armour for war.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again,' at opening — editorial collection marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps two cosmic entities to simile figures: the ship of the day → great spear, the Great Spirit → wise craftsman. Both sides remain within the cosmic system. The Great Spirit's role of beautifying and setting aright maps to its systematic cosmic function (cf. Gardner: 79.29-30, 102.27). Heavy lacunae obscure some content. Substrate score 7.69 is the highest in the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit is like a combatant who might go towards a king's son who has been taken prisoner of war, and he redeems him from the hands of his enemies.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again,' at opening — editorial collection marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Maps the Living Spirit's cosmic function (redeeming the First Man) to the simile of a combatant rescuing a king's son. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'King's son' = First Man, 'enemies' = powers of Darkness. Compact and systematic—no editorial extension. Substrate score 6.06.

paragraphs.core_text: [The Amba]ssador too is like a great man [ ... ] because of the treasure [ ... ] hand of his prisoners [ ... ] these light powers [ ... ... the] sons and their soul, so that they would [ ... ... (the soul) might] be brought forth in the land wherein it was imprisoned.
paragraphs.temporal_note: No dialogue frame marker—begins directly with the cosmic entity. Maps the Ambassador (Third Ambassador) to a simile figure, with the cosmic referent being the redemption of light powers / living soul from imprisonment. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. Heavily lacunose but the substrate structure is clear. Despite zero substrate vocabulary score (due to lacunae destroying diagnostic terms), the structure and content are fully substratic.

Clear pivot from impersonal cosmic teaching to direct audience address: 'Again he turned, and he says to his disciples' is dialogue frame; 'You yourselves must be purifiers and redeemers of your soul' is imperative exhortation; 'so that you may be counted to the company of the fathers of light... in the new aeon, in the place of joy' is eschatological promise. The cosmic redemption theme from the five parables is now APPLIED to the community's own situation—the mapping crosses from cosmos to contemporary audience. This is the devotional closure appended to the substrate teaching sequence.
